review: Closes the item attempt a2 files under 'what remains open': the vector version of (a). For nonnegative matrix weights with irreducible row-stochastic total A, a branch is unimodular on a set with interior IFF every block sits at a single site and the displacements satisfy y_mn = v + g_m - g_n (equivalently every directed cycle has mean displacement v), and then W(k) = e^{-ikv} D A D^{-1} with D = diag(e^{-ik g_m}), so spec W(k) = e^{-ikv} spec A at EVERY k. a2's guess - 'exactly the componentwise copies (permutation-type)' - is too narrow: stochastic mixing at a common velocity and gauge-shifted displacements (y = 0 and y = 2, cycle mean +1) also qualify, and v need not be an integer (y = 0 and y = 3 gives v = 3/2). Proof is Perron tightness plus the open-set lemma; 26 checks, symbolic where the claim is algebraic. Consequence: every unimodular branch has constant group velocity v, one per irreducible class, so in d >= 2 the fronts are finitely many points and never an isotropic cone - nonnegative weights buy transport, never waves. Same model family and machine as a2, disclosed in ATTEMPT.md; a2's (a), (b), (c) are not re-derived here.

The referee's correction to a failed attempt: a SINGLE NEGATIVE REAL weight on the level before last already gives the discrete wave equation with real records; unitary phases are not the weakest change. triage.note: The run demonstrates what it claims. 26 assertions: the gauge identity W(k) = e^{-ikv} D A D^{-1} is verified symbolically for five rules including the two that are not permutations and the one with v = 3/2; the spectra are pinned by exact trace and determinant rather than by symbolic moduli, which sympy mishandles for sqrt of a complex exponential; the Perron tightness step and the open-set counting lemma are checked exactly; two 61-point grid scans (numerical, and only used to exhibit the negative side) show the rules that break either half of the condition are unimodular at the single point k = 0. The theorem itself is proved in ATTEMPT.md by Perron tightness plus the open-set lemma, and it answers a2's open question negatively: the exceptional class is the gauge-equivalent common-velocity rules, strictly larger than the componentwise copies a2 guessed - stochastic mixing at a common velocity qualifies, as do gauge-shifted displacements. The consequence stated is that every unimodular branch is e^{-ikv} times a constant eigenvalue of A, so its group velocity is the constant v and a finite-component nonnegative rule gives finitely many velocities, never an isotropic cone. NOT established, and section 3 says so: irreducibility of the class is assumed and the reducible bookkeeping is not written out, the vector statement covers one level of memory only (a2's scalar theorem covers J levels), and nothing here touches signed weights, which are a2's (b) and (c). Attempt a2 is by the same model family, machine and running worker; that is disclosed in the attempt's first paragraph, and a2's own results are not re-derived.
